description: DeSciX Cloud Service Configuration Schema - Defines key categories for bootstrap and dev override

bootstrap_keys.description: Keys loaded from .env/.yaml BEFORE Secret Manager access (required for bootstrap)
bootstrap_keys._developer_credential_comment: DEVELOPER_WALLET_ADDRESS (public) + DEVELOPER_SIGNATURE (SECRET) added so an SDK-based app microservice (CEO-D-2026-06-02-APP-MICROSERVICE-IS-CLI-CLIENT-WALLET-SIG) can read the developer credential from process.env. In prod the SIGNATURE env var is mounted from a DEDICATED per-app Secret Manager secret via Cloud Run --set-secrets (keeps it OUT of the shared descix_config_{env}). Benign for other services: _loadBootstrapKeys only assigns when the env var is present.

required_keys.description: Keys that MUST resolve to a non-null value after bootstrap completes for EVERY cloud-core consumer. CloudConfig.initialize() throws CloudConfigFatalError if any of these are null/undefined. These are the UNIVERSAL base: FIRESTORE_DATABASE_ID (named-DB selector used by cloud-core's own CacheFirestore + ServiceManifest — a null silently writes to the wrong/default database) and GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID (auto-resolved at runtime from GCP ADC in initialize(); every cloud-core service runs on GCP). Platform-node-specific keys (RAG/AI/chain/content storage) were MOVED OUT per CEO-D-2026-06-01-APP-DEV-MODEL D1 — a lightweight SDK-based service that uses neither Pinecone/Gemini/AI/chain/GCS must not be coerced into declaring them. Services that DO need those keys declare them per-service via createCloudConfig({ additionalRequiredKeys: [...] }) (e.g. DeSciX_Cloud/daita). The hard-fail is preserved — only its scope moved (feedback_no_hardcoded_fallbacks STILL HOLDS). Add a key here ONLY if a null value would cause silent runtime degradation for ANY conceivable cloud-core consumer.

boolean_keys.description: Keys that should be parsed as boolean (value === 'true')

dev_override_keys.description: Keys that can be overridden via .env or dev-overrides.json in dev for pre-testing before Secret Manager deployment

defaults.description: Keys with safe default values. Use SPARINGLY — prefer null to expose config errors. Only add here if the value is stable across all environments and has no security implications.
